primitives.name: Temporal Transaction Kernel

primitives.name: Fee Assessment Regime
primitives.verbatim_quote: If you had insufficient available funds when a transaction posted, fees may have been assessed.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_{\\text{fee}}': 'assessed fee amount in USD', 'B_{\\text{avail}}': 'available balance before transaction in USD', 'T_{\\text{txn}}': 'transaction value in USD'}
primitives.assumptions: Fee F_fee is applied iff B_avail < T_txn, modeled as binary indicator function f(B_avail, T_txn).
primitives.breakdown_regime: When B_avail becomes negative or less than T_txn, F_fee > 0 triggers, causing discontinuous drop in B(t).

layer2.mapping: Fee kernel F(t) = f(B(t), T(t)) · α(t) where α(t) scales fee magnitude based on account type and time-dependent policy.
layer2.telemetry: Verification of F_fee against reported monthly service fee summary.

layer2.telemetry: Balance drifts between A_src and A_dst match documented transfer amounts.

The underlying state space consists of two hypotheses: the caller is genuinely Wells Fargo (true positive/negative) or a scammer (false positive/negative). The transition dynamics involve updating posterior probabilities after each verification step, guided by Bayes' rule. This aligns with GSI's goal of building robust predictive models for adversarial behavior by treating each interaction as a streaming data point for refining fraud likelihood estimates. The telemetry metrics serve as empirical priors in a hierarchical Bayesian framework, allowing the system to adapt to new attack vectors. From a GSE perspective, the document encodes a state-machine where the current state is the verified status of an entity, and transitions occur only upon successful completion of the verification protocol. The cross-layer veto condition ensures that the verification layer does not leak sensitive account information back to the potential attacker during the confirmation process, preventing feedback loops that could compromise the system.
